questions.question: Why does a plant change some glucose into starch?
questions.expected_answer: A plant makes more glucose than it needs right away. Glucose dissolves in water, so it is not good for storing. Starch does not dissolve, so it can be packed away and kept. When the plant needs energy, at night, in winter or to grow again, it breaks the starch back down into glucose.

questions.question: Give one example each of a stem, a root, a fruit and a seed that store food.
questions.expected_answer: Stem: potato or madumbe. Root: sweet potato, cassava or carrot. Fruit: banana, mango or pumpkin. Seed: maize, wheat, rice, sorghum or beans.

questions.question: Describe how to test a food for starch and what the results mean.
questions.expected_answer: Put a drop of brown iodine solution on the food. If it turns blue-black, the food contains starch. If it stays brown or yellow-brown, the food has no starch. Use only a drop and wash your hands afterwards.
